A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPGM research work and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v4 reports original OPGM and OPGM-rs experiments on image keypoint and PPI network matching, including performance, sensitivity, runtime, and failure analyses in Section 8 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–3, including the supplementary evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 7 revises the existing training loss: L_cost changes from +(1/m) times the log sum to -sum, and L_bias loses its 1/m and 1/n normalization factors. This corrects the cost term's optimization direction and changes loss scaling. The architecture, matching mask, transport objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged; implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pascal VOC Keypoint, SPair-71K, IMCPT 50/100, and yeast PPI matching with the same noise scenarios. No dataset, task, or test population is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same NGM-v2 and GCAN configurations using dummy, ILP, AFAT-U, and AFAT-I matching. The PPI comparisons retain SIGMA and StableGM, and the runtime comparison retains GCAN, AFAT-I, and AFAT-U.

E3.justification: Section 8 and Appendix B retain the same feature extraction, model backbones, evaluation metrics, hyperparameter searches, training budgets, and 3,000-pair inference-time evaluation. The loss revisions do not come with a reported change to the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The fixed-versus-learned matching-bias comparisons, rho and lambda sensitivity analyses, PPI noise tests, and Appendix B analysis of partiality and mismatching errors are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 8.1 retains five random starts and 95% confidence intervals for image keypoint matching. Uncertainty reporting in the tables and figures is unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–3 are unchanged. For example, OPGM-rs retains mean F1-scores of 57.8 ± 0.2 on SPair-71K and 72.7 ± 0.2 on IMCPT 100. No updated results accompany the revised loss formulas.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of L_cost and L_bias change through the sign and normalization revisions in Section 7. The optimal-transport definitions, theorem statements, assignment reduction, and all proofs in Appendix A remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: weighted optimal partial transport, exact assignment-based solutions with cubic worst-case complexity, and an end-to-end architecture with partial matching loss.

C2.justification: The explanations of matching biases, parameter sensitivity, and inference efficiency are unchanged. Section 9 and Appendix B retain the same limitations concerning ambiguous annotations, noise, and incorrectly excluded true matches.

D1.justification: Section 8 adds an explicit OPGM GitHub code-access pointer; v4 supplied only the ThinkMatch baseline-code pointer. Appendix B's implementation, hardware, optimizer, and hyperparameter information is unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, without verifying repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to previous graph matching and optimal transport approaches are unchanged. Rewording the baseline-results attribution does not alter that positioning.

P1.justification: Section 8 replaces 'training and testing efficiency' with 'runtime efficiency,' rephrases the baseline provenance sentence, and adds the code-availability sentence. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section organization and the remaining narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Page 8 has localized equation-spacing changes and text reflow around the revised losses and added code link. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–4 retain identical content, captions, styling, and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects the cost-loss sign so minimization favors the intended matching behavior and adds a direct code-access pointer, improving the written specification and reproducibility guidance. The normalization changes remain unexplained, and the PDFs do not clarify which loss produced the unchanged experimental results. The supported overall gain is therefore limited.
